To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a home based, telephone supported problem solving training program is effective in reducing depression, health complaints and dysfunctional problem solving styles, but not in improving caregiver well being, among family caregivers of community residing persons with TBI

a problem solving intervention was effective in reducing depression, health complaints and dysfunctional problem solving styles in a group of family caregivers of individuals with traumatic brain injury.

a 4 session problem solving training program, provided in the home and followed by 8 telephone calls over the course 12 months, was effective in alleviating depression, health complaints and dysfunctional problem solving styles reported by family caregivers of persons who sustained traumatic brain injuries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and implementation of a family based intervention for family members of persons with TBRIs that is designed to reduce the burden of caregiving and to increase well being among family members.
the development and validation of a model for the assessment of problem solving ability in the elderly.

how family caregivers of persons who have sustained traumatic brain injuries (TBI) manage their caregiving responsibilities, the stressors that they encounter in their daily lives, and the impact that these stressors and the management of their caregiving have on them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
problem solving training is effective in decreasing distress among caregivers of persons with TBIs.
problem solving skills training is effective in reducing depression, health complaints and dysfunctional problem solving styles in family caregivers of persons living with a TBI.
problem solving training provided in a community setting to family caregivers of persons living with TBI was effective in alleviating depressive symptoms and in reducing health complaints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that problem solving training is effective in reducing caregiver burden.
problem solving training provided in a family caregiver's home is effective in decreasing depression, health complaints and dysfunctional problem solving styles in caregivers.
the problem solving training program is effective for reducing depression, burden, and health complaints among family caregivers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
family caregivers can learn problem solving skills and these skills can reduce their distress and improve their well-being.
family caregivers of persons living with a TBI can learn to problem solve more effectively, and in so doing, they can reduce their own stress and burden.
family members can be taught to solve problems more effectively, and this training has a significant impact on their well-being and the well-being of the person with TBI.
